This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e cour
 following:
 Order
1.
Heard on IA No.1012 of 2020, which is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the appeal.

Vinod vs Kusharg on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143373902/
1
2. Delay of 182 days has properly been explained by the appellant and the application is well supported by the affidavit.
3. On due consideration, IA is allowed and the delay of 182 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
4. In this matter liability of the insurance company is not disputed.
5. With the consent of both the parties, matter is heard finally.

6. This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short "MV Act") being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 8.5.2019 passed in MACC Case No.300128/2016 by the 2nd Addl. Member, MACT, West Nimar,
Mandleshwar (M.P.) for enhancement of the compensation amount.

7. The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that on 18.7.2016 at about 12.45 p.m.
appellant/claimant Vinod along with Kundan were going on a motorcycle, at that time the offending vehicle bearing registration No.MP09- CR-0200 which was driven by the respondent No.1 rashly and negligently, dashed the motorcycle of appellant, due to which Vinod and Kundan both fell down on the floor and Vinod sustained several injuries over different parts of his body.
Rod has been implanted in his tibia, fibula and femur bone and finally his right leg above knee was amputated.
Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.
8. Appellant/claimant in his claim petition has submitted that he was remained admitted in the hospital from 18.7.2016 to 28.7.2016.
Appellant was aged about 27 years at the time of accident and he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Hence claim petition was filed before the below Tribunal for compensation of Rs.35,00,000/-.
9. Respondents No.1 & 2 were absent before the Tribunal, therefore, matter has been proceeded ex parte against them.

10. Respondent No.3/insurance company by denying the averments made in the claim petition has submitted that at the time of accident Kundan was driving the motorcycle bearing registration No.MP41-3961 rashly and negligently and due to his self-negligence, they fell down on the breaker and sustained injuries.
No accident has been done by the offending vehicle.

11. The below Tribunal after framing the issues, directed both the parties to adduce their evidence and after appreciation of the evidence, awarded the compensation of Rs.11,04,874/- in favour of the appellant with interest @8% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, appellant has preferred this miscellaneous appeal for enhancement of the compensation amount.
12. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned award passed by the below Tribunal is against the law and facts.

She submits that the below Tribunal has not considered the Vinod vs Kusharg on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143373902/
2 fact that victim has suffered 100% permanent disability in the right leg.

entities.text: Vinod vs Kusharg on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The tribunal has not awarded adequate amount under the head of Special Diet, Transportation and Attendant.
Hence she prays that the impugned award be modified and the compensation amount be enhanced.

13. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurance company opposes the prayer by submitting that the impugned award passed by the below Tribunal is just, proper and adequate and not deserve for any interference.
14.
Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the entire record with due care.

15. From oral evidence of claimant Vinod and the other documentary evidence available on record, it is proved that the accident took place by the offending vehicle which was being driven by the respondent No.1 at the time of accident and offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.3.
Before the below Tribunal respondent No.3 did not examine any witness.

Therefore, on the basis of the evidence available on record, it is proved that accident took place by the offending vehicle, which was driven by the respondent No.1 and at that time offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.
There is no evidence available on record to establish that there was any breach of the insurance policy committed by the owner or driver of the offending vehicle.

16. The moot question to be addressed in this appeal preferred by the appellant/claimant is that, as to whether the Tribunal was justified in awarding the compensation of Rs.11,04,874/- to the appellant.

17. Appellant Vinod (PW-1) before the below Tribunal deposed that at the time of accident his age was 27 years and he was earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month and his whole family is dependent upon him.

Due to the accident his right leg above the knee has been amputated,
therefore, he became permanent disabled and unable to perform any work.
His statement is well supported by the Kundan (PW-2) and Dr. Ashish Mehrotra (PW-3).

Respondent No.3/insurance company in rebuttal did not examine any witness, therefore, no reason to disbelieve the appellant's witnesses and disability certificate Ex.P/2777 & P/278, which has been issued by the District Medical Board.
Therefore, below tribunal right held that victim sustained 80% permanent disability.

18. The tribunal has awarded Rs.2,19,714/- towards actual medical expenses, Rs.10,000/- for special died, attendant & transportation, Rs.15,000/-
for pain and suffering and Rs.8,60,160/- under the head of permanent disability.
As per the opinion of the medical board appellant has suffered 80% permanent disability.

The accident is of the year 2016, therefore considering the year of accident and nature of work and guidelines issued by the Labour Department of M.P. Government, the tribunal ought to have assessed the monthly income of the appellant as Rs.5,350/-.
The tribunal has correctly applied the multiplier of 16 and rightly added 40% towards the loss of future prospects.

Therefore, compensation for the permanent disability comes to Rs.5350 x 12 = 64,200/- ( ) Rs.25,680/- (40% future prospects) = Rs.89,880/- x 80% x 16 (multiplier) = Rs.11,50,464/-, whereas the below tribunal has awarded only Rs.8,60,160/- under Vinod vs Kusharg on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143373902/
3
this head, therefore, the appellant is entitled for further sum of Rs.2,90,304/- under the head of permanent disability.
The amount awarded to the appellant under the head of special diet, attendant and transportation are also not adequate, hence in these heads appellant is entitled to a further sum of Rs.10,000/-.
The rest of amounts awarded by the tribunal under other heads are just and proper.
19. Thus, the appeal is partly allowed.
The appellant is awarded further sum of Rs.3,00,304/- over and above the amount awarded by the tribunal.
The enhanced amount will bear interest at the same rate, as awarded by the tribunal and will be governed by the same conditions as contained in the impugned award of tribunal.
20. The miscellaneous appeal is accordingly disposed of.
C.C. as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE trilok Vinod vs Kusharg on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143373902/
